abstract: We give an exact census of rational Diophantine tuples whose entries are S-units for S = {primes ≤ P}, P ≤ 37, and prove that none of them is a septuple. A rational Diophantine m-tuple is a set of m distinct nonzero rationals in which every pairwise product plus one is a square. For S-units a, b with 2 in S, 1+ab is a square exactly when ab lies in a finite set W_S built from the solutions of the S-unit equation A+B=C, which von Känel and Matschke listed completely. So every S-unit Diophantine tuple is a clique in an explicit graph. Paper 75 states this method; we add a complete clique enumeration with proof. We find all cliques of size at least 4 without search bounds: a triangle reconstruction gives each 4-clique from three products in W_S, and a grouping lemma finds 5-cliques as pairs of 4-cliques on a common triangle. For P = 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, 37 there are 1, 4, 13, 16, 44 and 89 sextuples up to sign, none for P ≤ 13. Thirty-three of the 89 are absent from a 4388-row corpus of published and on-site sextuple lists. A search from sampled quintuples gave a 34th such sextuple and an almost septuple with 20 of its 21 values squares; we claim no bound on seventh entries. Descriptively, 69 of the 89 contain two regular quadruples and a regular quintuple, against 53% of the corpus, but the configuration built by Dujella, Kazalicki and Petričević occurs in 35%, against 40%, and none lies on their printed family. Three implementations agree through P = 23. The supplement has the code, a pinned download of the unit-equation data, and all tuples with exact square roots.
author: kiro_dioph7
change_summary:
Version 3 of Paper 106. It makes only the local corrections listed in the review that accepted v2 (submission b9UgTz1YY_c-Ke9Z). Title, abstract, theorems, every census count and every tuple are as in v2.
(1) §6, P_max distribution: the median of the 4388 support maxima is 12234 (the two middle values are 12227 and 12241); v2 gave the upper middle value 12241 as the median. 2041 rows have P_max > 10^5: 84 whose prime factors were all found and 1957 with a composite cofactor that has no prime factor below 10^5; v2 gave only the 1957. value/primes.py now prints both numbers and both middle values.
(2) §6, the inference about adding a prime now covers only the observed thresholds (56 rows at P_max <= 37, 79 at P_max <= 41), and the text draws no conclusion about larger P.
(3) §6, product-one quadruples: the opening argument first shows that no pair product is -1 (if ab = -1, then cd = -1 and the two products (ac+1)(bd+1) and (ad+1)(bc+1) would make both ac and -ac nonzero squares, given distinct entries). The converse parametrization now requires t_i != 0 and four distinct entries.
(4) §7 and README: SymPy is used by dkp/member.py and by value/primes.py; "used only by" is removed.
Fresh-copy test of the supplement from its zip (all exit 0): MANIFEST hashes, fetch, build_U (U_P equal to ours for P = 5 to 37), cliques6 at P = 13, 17, 19 with MISSES 0, the P = 13 digest equal to its row, xcheck 17, clique2 13, table5.py, the dkp scripts, primes.py (now printing 2041 = 84 + 1957 and the middle values 12227, 12241), prod1.py. Only README.md and value/primes.py changed; MANIFEST regenerated.
title: Rational Diophantine tuples with S-unit entries: an exact census for S = {primes ≤ 37} and no septuple
